newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to invest $1.3 billion more in Detroit. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to invest $1.3 billion more in Detroit. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]

text.p: Chrysler Corp., moving to boost capacity for popular Jeep and truck models, said Wednesday it plans new investments of $1.3 billion in six Detroit manufacturing plants over the next five years.

The investments, part of the company's five-year programme to spend more than $22 billion on new products, will lead to "hundreds of new jobs" for the city, Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton told a news conference.
"This is a commitment to our workers, our facilities and the city of Detroit," Eaton said.
However, the announcements did little to help resolve a labour dispute at a Chrysler engine plant in Detroit that is not in line for any new investments.

United Auto Workers Local 51 at Chrysler's Mound Road engine plant, which builds V-6, V-8 and V-10 truck engines, has threatened to strike at 11:59 p.m. EDT Wednesday unless Chrysler agrees to drop plans to shift driveshaft production to outside suppliers -- a move that could cost the plant more than 200 jobs.

The 1,800-employee Mound Road plant's future is uncertain, because most of its products will be phased out after Chrysler launches production of a new generation of truck engines next year at the new Mack Avenue Engine Plant, which will get a $150 million investment boost.

Eaton declined to say how many additional vehicles the new investments will allow Chrysler to build, adding that production and employment levels will be determined by vehicle demand. He said the investments are a small step toward Chrysler's goal of boosting total global production capacity to 3.8 million units by the year 2000 from 3.2 million for the 1997 model year.
Chrysler now employs more than 9,800 hourly production workers within the Detroit city limits, more than either Ford Motor Co. or General Motors Corp.

The centrepiece of the investments is a $750 million expansion of Chrysler's Jefferson North Assembly Plant, which analysts estimate will boost Chrysler's straight time production capacity for Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles to 375,000 from about 260,000 currently.
The $150 million for Mack Avenue Engine, which brings Chrysler's total investment in the facility to $900 million, will pay for technological improvements and capacity increases.
Chrysler also announced it would invest $300 million in its Detroit Axle plant to boost capacity for truck axles, allowing it to boost production of its popular Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks.

Chrysler also will invest $100 million (Corrects figure from $150 million) in its McGraw Glass Plant, a facility it tried to sell last year, to prepare it to make glass for new models. Chrysler in late 1995 gave up on plans to sell the plant because of union objections. It agreed to make new investments in the facility as part of a deal to settle a four-day strike in November 1995.

The automaker is investing $10 million (Corrects figure from $100 million) in its Conner Avenue Assembly Plant to prepare it for production of the Plymouth Prowler, while the Mt. Elliott Tool and Die Plant will get $3 million for infrastructure improvements.
The announcement brings Chrysler's total investment in the city of Detroit to $3.8 billion since it rebuilt the Jefferson North Assembly Plant, which opened in 1992.
The company has added 2,100 Chrysler jobs in the city since 1994, when it added its third shift at the Jefferson North facility.

The Chrysler investments, along with plans by General Motors Corp. to relocate thousands of employees to its new headquarters in Detroit's downtown Renaissance Centre, improving the city's automotive employment outlook for the first time in years.
City officials hope that the Big Three's leadership will encourage other companies to invest in the city and help reverse decades of decay.
Mayor Dennis Archer on Wednesday lauded Chrysler's "extraordinary corporate citizenship" and added a sales pitch.
"When your are thinking about buying your next car, I want you to remember who's investing in this city. Buy Chrysler, buy Ford, buy General Motors."
